author: WP18
summary: Updated-for-d6e9ff05 chapter on Android and Apple evidence: the Android application structure and NDK code, recorded emulator runs, mobile lifecycle policy, the asset route, the Metal renderer's seams and the macOS/iOS workflows. Several claims are stale: CNA uses JNI for asset lookup, LowMemory only logs, ContentManager handles Android packaged assets, and tvOS is refused at configure time. The platforms guide and Development pages had the status; the structure, lifecycle table, asset route and workflow checks are on a new deep dive.

concepts.text: Platform support is a ladder (platform branches, cross-compile, emulator, package, frame, real hardware); Android has recorded emulator evidence of an earlier revision, macOS/iOS routes are declared in workflows, and tvOS is not implemented.
tokens: Platform support is not one fact

concepts.text: Target OS, platform implementation and renderer stay separate: Android and Apple use the SDL3 implementation, iOS is a target OS rather than a CNA_PLATFORM value, the iOS smoke uses SDL_RENDERER and METAL is macOS-only.
tokens: iOS is not a CNA_PLATFORM value

concepts.text: The Devices demo is a complete 39-file Gradle/NDK application (wrapper, manifest, DemodevicesActivity as an SDLActivity subclass, SDL Java glue, launcher resources, native build descriptions).

Its CMake route (Gradle property BUILD_WITH_CMAKE; ndk-build is the default) forces tests/examples off and add_subdirectory()s the CNA root so the APK compiles CNA; it pins compile/target SDK 35, NDK 30.0.14904198, min SDK 24 and arm64-v8a only.
concepts.note: Corrected: the CMake route is opt-in; the default Gradle route is ndk-build.

concepts.text: The Android-specific production code is concentrated in the NDK sensor layer (about 3,300 lines across four sources and six headers; the older text said about 2,090) using ASensorManager, ALooper and event queues.
concepts.note: Line count re-measured at TARGET including headers.

concepts.text: Each AndroidSensorBridge owns a worker std::thread and the Motion backend aggregates six bridges, so one thread-construction site yields up to six concurrent workers per Motion instance.
The older text said CNA itself uses no JNI; at TARGET the SDL3 file service uses JNI (SDL_GetAndroidJNIEnv, AssetManager.list) to resolve packaged asset names case-insensitively.
tokens: CNA does use JNI, in one place

concepts.text: The Devices module's only Android link is android and log (PUBLIC), and portable sensor maths stays outside __ANDROID__ guards so native tests exercise it while only the I/O boundary is gated.
On 4 July 2026 an NDK-built CnaTests ran on an AVD and passed 230 networking and 1,831 other cases before a TitleContainer test crashed without an Activity.
concepts.note: Campaign result of an earlier revision; no machine-readable record of it exists in the TARGET tree.

concepts.text: CNA's notes record a 7.3 MB debug APK of the Devices demo installed and launched on the Medium_Phone emulator with console-injected sensor values; only SDL's accelerometer/gyroscope delivery was driven, not the Compass/Motion NDK bridges.

No APK, AAB, logcat, Android screenshot or machine-readable result is retained and no CNA binary has a record on physical Android hardware, so the honest wording is recorded emulator execution of an earlier revision.
tokens: recorded emulator execution of an earlier revision

concepts.text: Android graphics uses the default SDL_RENDERER; WEBGPU is the only renderer with an explicit Android native-window surface path and has no record of running there.

concepts.section: Lifecycle coverage is explicit but partial
concepts.text: The platform contract carries WillEnterBackground, DidEnterForeground, LowMemory and Terminating; Game suspends between the first two (resetting the clock and invalidating the surface on resume), only logs LowMemory (the older text said it triggers content cleanup) and exits on Terminating.

concepts.section: Lifecycle coverage is explicit but partial
concepts.text: Lifecycle handling is source policy plus a portable test (GameTest.MobileLifecycleEventsSuspendResumeAndTerminateTheLoop); nothing drives background, foreground, low memory and process recreation on a device or emulator or checks graphics-resource survival.

concepts.section: Assets expose a deeper integration gap
concepts.text: The older text said ContentManager builds Content/<asset> from the working directory and never reaches the Android fallback; at TARGET, under __ANDROID__, relative paths go to the packaged-asset namespace through the platform's TryLoadFileIgnoringCase, and TitleContainer tries std::filesystem then the Android asset name.

concepts.section: Assets expose a deeper integration gap
concepts.text: A historical run found the TitleContainer SDL_LoadFile fallback could segfault without a real Activity/JNI context.
concepts.note: Reported for an earlier revision; no TARGET record or test reproduces it.

concepts.section: Assets expose a deeper integration gap
concepts.text: No CNA code places the content root in an Apple bundle's Resources directory and the Apple smoke apps load no content, so bundle content layout must be arranged and tested by the application through ContentManager.
tokens: No CNA code chooses an application bundle's Resources directory

concepts.section: Assets expose a deeper integration gap
concepts.text: StorageDevice on Android asks Sharp Runtime's storage policy for the package-private files directory (SDL_GetAndroidInternalStoragePath, fallback /data/local/tmp) because HOME is undefined and the working directory is not writable.
METAL's Objective-C++ .mm sources and the AppKit, Metal, QuartzCore and Foundation frameworks enter the build only when METAL is the configured renderer; source isolation is not native validation.

The Metal CTest prefix includes host-portable policy tests (Metal_PortableHelpers) registered whenever tests are on, so ctest -R '^Metal' passes on Linux without Apple code; only Metal_Smoke and Metal_Capabilities need a METAL build, and quoted results need the build's renderer identity.
A macOS 14 / Xcode 15.4 workflow on the Metal renderer's original feature tree ran 143 tests (136 passed, 7 failed) before the later adaptation.
concepts.note: Result for a pre-adaptation feature branch; interfaces and registration changed afterwards.

concepts.text: At TARGET metal-macos-ci configures METAL with validation variables and runs the Metal prefix, and apple-ci builds an SDL_RENDERER CnaTests suite and a self-contained .app whose Mach-O dependencies are checked with otool -L before it is launched for CNA_APPLE_SMOKE_OK; these are declared gates, not retrieved run records.

concepts.section: iOS: final-link and simulator route; tvOS remains a non-claim
concepts.text: The iOS route is ios.cmake plus a smoke app (Game, GraphicsDeviceManager, RunOneFrame) final-linked for arm64 device and simulator with tests, examples and net off; the workflow checks LC_BUILD_VERSION, the SDL_main export and build-machine dependencies, then ad-hoc signs, installs and launches the simulator bundle for the one-frame marker; no physical device.

concepts.section: iOS: final-link and simulator route; tvOS remains a non-claim
concepts.text: The older text treated tvOS as a mere non-claim; at TARGET ApplePlatform.cmake refuses tvOS, watchOS and visionOS with a configure error naming the two supported Apple targets.
tokens: tvOS, watchOS and visionOS fail configuration

concepts.section: iOS: final-link and simulator route; tvOS remains a non-claim
concepts.text: Next evidence steps are narrow and each should state its rung: an archived Android graphics build and emulator frame, retained Apple/Metal workflow artifacts, a physical iOS result, and a designed (not inferred) tvOS host.
tokens: should say which rung it proves

issues.text: Android has no workflow or preset; the only execution records are emulator runs of an earlier revision with no retained artifacts, and content loading through ContentManager inside an APK is untested.
Mobile lifecycle handling is covered only by a portable test; no device or emulator test drives background, foreground, low memory or process recreation.
iOS evidence is a device final-link and one simulator frame; no physical device run exists, and tvOS/watchOS/visionOS are refused at configure time.
ctest -R '^Metal' matches host-portable Metal_PortableHelpers on any host, so a Metal pass without the renderer identity is ambiguous evidence (a design choice).
No CNA code resolves an Apple application bundle's Resources directory for content; a relative content root depends on the working directory and SDL's file-open rules, untested for a launched bundle.
